Question 22 [6 marks]: In relation to human rights, discuss the extent to which the Australian Constitution reflects changing values and ethical standards.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 6):
6 marks: Provides a thorough discussion of the extent to which the Australian Constitution reflects changing social values and ethical standards
4–5 marks: Provides a sound discussion of the extent to which the Australian Constitution reflects changing social values and ethical standards
2–3 marks: Provides some discussion of the extent to which the Australian Constitution reflects changing social values and ethical standards
1 marks: Provides some relevant information

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
The Australian Constitution, established in 1901, provides a framework to reflect changing values and ethical standards through judicial interpretation, referendums and legislative reforms. The few explicit rights identified in the Constitution, such as the right to freedom of religion (Section 116) arguably leave gaps in protection. Further, the Constitution does not list what the Australian values are. Due to the complexity of the process, Constitutional reform is not often accomplished, for example the 1988 Rights and Freedoms referendum which aimed at enshrining civil rights failed. Conversely, the Constitution does allow the High Court to uphold implied rights and adapt to changing values. This occurred in the 1997 case, Lange v Australia Broadcasting Corporation, which upheld the existence of freedom of political communication. Additionally, the Constitution provides a framework to reflect changing values and ethical standards, however, has limitations due to the complexity of the reform progress.
